45:
The study "Ask Iska and IskOU: Analysis of UPOU's Chatbot for Information Support Services" investigates the performance and user satisfaction of two AI chatbots, Iska and IskOU, developed by the University of the Philippines Open University. These tools aim to streamline information support for students, faculty, and the public via Facebook and the university website. Using a mixed-methods approach, researchers collected data from forty-one respondents and evaluated the chatbots based on response time, multi-thread conversation, maxim of quantity, perceived ease of use, and the recognition of user goals and intent.

Findings regarding performance were mixed. The chatbots performed exceptionally well in response time, with 100% of respondents reporting prompt answers and an average response time of 900 milliseconds. Users found the tools intuitive, reporting high levels of perceived ease of use and usefulness. However, significant limitations were identified regarding the chatbots' ability to interpret intent. While successful at answering frequently asked questions regarding application procedures and program lists, they struggled with complex or highly specific queries. Approximately 24.4% of users reported the chatbot "sometimes" answered completely, while 22% reported it "never" answered completely.

The study concludes that while the chatbots are successful for high-volume, repetitive tasks, they are not yet a complete replacement for human support. Researchers suggest expanding the knowledge base, improving the ability to provide direct answers rather than external links, and implementing monitoring schemes to track unresolved queries.
